title: Functorial transport to a finite field
statement:
Fix a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi$, and the integral constructible categories and their raw rationalizations $\Dbc(T,E)$ of [def-weil-pbc-rational-category]. Every exact $\mathcal O_E$-linear functor $F:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ between these integral categories [def-weil-linear-functor, def-weil-triangulated-category] has a unique $E$-linear extension $F_E:\mathcal C[1/\varpi]\to\mathcal D[1/\varpi]$ agreeing with $F$ on objects and integral morphisms. This extension is exact, with the localized shift comparison. For two such exact $\mathcal O_E$-linear functors $F,G:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$, every natural transformation $\eta:F\Rightarrow G$ extends uniquely with components $\eta_K\otimes1$.

In particular, let $X,Y,X',Y'$ be schemes for which these integral constructible categories are defined. Suppose the integral operations denoted $Rf_*:\Dbc(X,\mathcal O_E)\to\Dbc(Y,\mathcal O_E)$, $Rf'_*:\Dbc(X',\mathcal O_E)\to\Dbc(Y',\mathcal O_E)$, $Lg^*_{\mathrm{comp}}:\Dbc(Y,\mathcal O_E)\to\Dbc(Y',\mathcal O_E)$ and $Lg'^*_{\mathrm{comp}}:\Dbc(X,\mathcal O_E)\to\Dbc(X',\mathcal O_E)$ are given exact $\mathcal O_E$-linear functors, together with a specified integral natural exchange $\Ex^{\mathrm{comp}}:Lg^*_{\mathrm{comp}}Rf_*\Rightarrow Rf'_*Lg'^*_{\mathrm{comp}}$. They extend to exact functors on the corresponding $\Dbc(-,E)$, and that specified exchange extends to a natural transformation between their composites, with component $\Ex^{\mathrm{comp}}_K\otimes1$. This is a transport assertion for supplied integral data, not an assertion that arbitrary scheme morphisms preserve integral constructibility.

proof.text: Write $R=\mathcal O_E$. By [def-weil-pbc-rational-category] and [def-weil-linear-scalar-localization], objects are unchanged and each Hom is $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C}(K,L)\otimes_R E$. Since $F$ is $R$-linear [def-weil-linear-functor], [def-weil-module-base-change] defines $F_E(K)=F(K)$ and $F_E(u\otimes a)=F(u)\otimes a$. The tensor balancing relation is respected because $F(ru)\otimes a=rF(u)\otimes a=F(u)\otimes ra$.

proof.text: Composition in [def-weil-linear-scalar-localization] gives $F_E((v\otimes b)\circ(u\otimes a))=F(vu)\otimes ba=(F(v)\otimes b)\circ(F(u)\otimes a)$. Extend this equality by bilinearity to finite sums of tensors. The identity goes to $F(\mathrm{id}_K)\otimes1=\mathrm{id}_{F(K)}\otimes1$. Any $E$-linear extension agreeing on integral morphisms must send $u\otimes a=a(u\otimes1)$ to $a(F(u)\otimes1)$; tensors generate the Hom module, proving uniqueness.

source.place: Proof: explicit expansion of localization functoriality

proof.text: For $\eta:F\Rightarrow G$ put $(\eta_E)_K=\eta_K\otimes1$. For a pure tensor $u\otimes a:K\to L$, its naturality equation is $(G(u)\circ\eta_K)\otimes a=(\eta_L\circ F(u))\otimes a$, the integral naturality equation tensored with $a$. Additivity proves it for every morphism. Since all objects are integral objects, the required components determine the transformation uniquely. Identity transformations and composites are preserved componentwise. The localized composite functor equals the composite of localized functors by the same formula on $u\otimes a$.

source.place: Proof: explicit expansion of localization functoriality

proof.text: Use [lem-weil-linear-scalar-localization-triangulated] for source and target: every distinguished rational triangle is isomorphic to $Q(T)$ for an integral distinguished triangle $T$. Localize the shift comparison of $F$ by step 3; its inverse also localizes and remains inverse. Now $F_E(Q(T))=Q(F(T))$ with this shift comparison. Since $F$ is exact, $F(T)$ is distinguished, so its image is distinguished by the cited lemma. Images of triangle isomorphisms remain isomorphisms, proving exactness on every distinguished rational triangle, as required by [def-weil-triangulated-category].

proof.text: Apply steps 1–4 separately to the four given exact $\mathcal O_E$-linear integral functors. For composites, the extension sends $u\otimes a$ to $F(G(u))\otimes a$, which is also the composite of the two extended functors. The given integral exchange therefore extends by step 3 to the transformation between these composites with component $\Ex^{\mathrm{comp}}_K\otimes1$. Its naturality for $u\otimes a$ is exactly the given integral naturality equation tensored with $a$, and then extends to sums. Thus the conclusion concerns the specified exchange, with no new choice of comparison map.
